rationale: 306.7 states the old planeswalker damage-redirection rule was removed, so a mode that deals damage to a player can never hit a planeswalker; 700.2d states a repeated mode may reuse the same target, so Nico is the only legal choice.

Group 1 is the legality of the attacker choices Master Warcraft's controller makes (508.1a chosen-creature requirements, 508.1c restrictions). Group 2 is 508.1d, which states a player isn't required to pay a cost a creature needs in order to attack.

702.37e/116.2b state that turning a face-down permanent face up is a special action whose payment is the morph cost, so mana restricted to turning a face-down permanent face up covers the whole increased cost; 118.8 states additional costs attach to spells being cast and abilities being activated, not to special actions.

The answer rests on the mana ability being controlled by the player who activated it, which is what False Dawn's 'abilities you control' checks; 113.8 and 405.4 each state that the controller of an activated ability is the player who activated it.

605.1a states a mana ability must be an activated ability meeting its criteria, and 113.3b states activated abilities are written '[Cost]: [Effect]'; Channel's mana-adding instruction is neither, so Phyrexian Revoker doesn't stop it.
729.1b states that no effect created in the main game has any meaning in the subgame, which is exactly why Word of Command's control effect doesn't carry into Shahrazad's subgame.
609.4a states that when two effects let a player do the same thing 'as though' different conditions were true, both conditions apply, which is the whole of the answer.

502.3 states the untap turn-based action in which the active player determines which permanents untap and untaps them; Undiscovered Paradise's return happens as part of that action, independent of whether it actually untaps.

701.27a states a double-faced permanent transforms by turning over; 707.8 states a copy of a double-faced permanent uses the copiable values of the face that's up, so it stays a copy of Ulrich's front face; 701.27e states a 'transforms into [something]' trigger triggers if the object has that characteristic immediately after transforming.

303.4f states that an Aura entering the battlefield from a non-stack zone has its controller choose a legal object to enchant; 115.1b states an Aura permanent doesn't target anything, which is why Deft Duelist's shroud is irrelevant.
116.2c states the special action of taking a later action to end a continuous effect; that effect, and so the {U} action, doesn't exist until Gliding Licid's activated ability has resolved.

208.3 states a noncreature permanent has no power, and 107.2 states that a number that can't be determined is treated as 0; Kobolds' power is still less than or equal to 0, so Old Man of the Sea's duration isn't over.

608.2h states that information about an object that's left the public zone it was expected to be in comes from its last known information, i.e. its toughness on the battlefield; 120.3e states damage is merely marked on a creature and doesn't reduce toughness.

723.1 states a player-controlling effect applies to the next turn the affected player actually takes and lasts the whole turn; 500.7 states extra turns are added directly after the specified turn, which fixes the Bishop/Charlotte/Charlotte ordering.

305.9 states that an object that's both a land and another card type is played as a land while still having that other type, so Dryad Arbor is a creature played by an opponent and Uphill Battle's replacement applies.

603.6d states 'as this enters' text is a static ability whose effect happens as part of the event that puts the permanent onto the battlefield; 614.17a, or 614.4 for replacement effects generally, states such effects must exist before that event, and Solemnity's doesn't because it enters simultaneously.

Same trace: 603.6d puts Phylactery Lich's counter placement inside its enter-the-battlefield event, and 614.17a/614.4 state the effect stopping counters must have stopped existing before that event, which sacrificing Suncleanser as Hellkite Hatchling enters can't achieve.

603.6d makes the counter part of Phylactery Lich's entry event; 614.17a/614.4 state the 'can't' effect is judged immediately before that event, when Tatterkite still had its ability because Humility entered at the same time.
608.2c states a spell's instructions are followed in the order written, so Leonin Arbiter is exiled, ending its effect, before the search instruction is carried out.

603.10a states leaves-the-battlefield abilities look back in time, so Slimefoot's trigger sees the state before the simultaneous deaths; 702.15c states last known information determines whether the damage source had lifelink.

708.2a states a face-down permanent is a 2/2 with no text, so Blightsteel Colossus had no replacement ability while on the battlefield; 614.4 states a replacement effect must exist before the event it would modify.
702.51a states convoke lets a creature be tapped for each mana in the spell's total cost and no more; 601.2h states the player pays the total cost, with no partial or extra payment.
608.2n states an instant or sorcery is put into its owner's graveyard only as the final part of its resolution, so Beacon Bolt isn't in the graveyard while it counts cards there.

Both state that an 'attacks' trigger triggers only when the creature is declared as an attacker; a creature put onto the battlefield attacking was never declared, so Scourge of the Throne doesn't trigger.

701.44a is the explore process, including putting the revealed card into the graveyard, which changes Volrath's Shapeshifter's text; 701.44b states the permanent explores only after that process completes, so the new trigger condition already exists.

603.2 states an ability triggers whenever a game event or game state matches its trigger event, which is checked against the objects as they exist after the surveil, when Blood Operative is already in the graveyard.

608.2c states Merfolk Trickster's instructions are followed in the order written, so the tap happens before abilities are lost; 603.2/113.7a state the ability triggers at that moment and then exists independently of its source.

112.1 states a spell is a card on the stack, so Soulfire Grand Master's grant to instant and sorcery spells never reaches Kozilek's Return in the graveyard; 113.3c states its second ability is a triggered ability, not a cast spell.

603.3b states the controller chooses the order in which their simultaneously triggered abilities go on the stack; 608.2d states choices offered by a resolving ability, such as paying Mentor's {1}, are announced during resolution, not when it's put on the stack.

603.12 states the discard creates a reflexive triggered ability that deals the damage; 608.2h/702.15c state that whether that source had lifelink is determined from Hypothesizzle's last known information on the stack.

603.3a states Crafty Cutpurse's enters trigger is controlled by whoever controlled it when it triggered, which is Nylah after Gather Specimens changed where it entered, and 109.5 states 'your' on that ability means that controller, so the token is created under Nylah's control.
202.1b states land cards have no mana cost; 118.6 states no mana cost is an unpayable cost and that attempting to pay an unpayable cost is illegal, so Illusionary Mask can't mask Dryad Arbor.

603.2d states an effect saying an ability triggers an additional time makes it trigger that many times, which is Traveling Chocobo; 607.2a states the linked second ability refers to all cards exiled by the first, so both exiled creatures' power and toughness count.

614.10/614.1b state that skipping a turn is a replacement effect and that a turn can no longer be skipped once it has started, so the choice happens before the turn begins; 723.1 states the control effect applies to that turn only once it begins.

608.2h states that when a resolving spell needs information about an object that isn't in the public zone it was expected to be in, last known information is used; either way the card's name is still Marble Diamond, which is all Predict checks.

616.1 states the affected object's controller chooses which replacement effect to apply, and 616.1b states an effect modifying under whose control the object would enter must be chosen first, which is why Xantcha's control change applies before Essence of the Wild's copy effect.

109.2 states that an object description using a card type or subtype without 'card' or a named zone means a permanent on the battlefield, so Pulmonic Sliver's grant reaches only Slivers on the battlefield.
500.7 states that effects giving extra turns add them directly after the specified turn; a turn created by Savor the Moment is such an extra turn, which is what Medomai's restriction refers to.

701.19a states a regeneration shield replaces only the next destruction this turn; 608.2c states Austere Command's chosen modes are carried out in the order written, so the shield is spent on the artifact destruction and is gone for the creature destruction.

115.7b describes changing a target of a spell, and 603.2e states 'becomes' triggers fire only when the state actually changes and don't retrigger while it persists, so Spellskite, already a target, doesn't become a target again.

616.1 states that when several replacement effects would modify an event the affected object's controller chooses the order; 616.1f states the process repeats over the modified event, so Furnace of Rath either doubles first or drops out entirely.

707.2c/707.2b state that a copy effect from a static ability locks in copiable values when it starts to apply and later changes to the original don't update the copy; 712.9 states only permanents represented by double-faced cards or tokens can transform, so Colossapede can't.

805.4b states each player on a team draws during the team's draw step and 805.6a states the team chooses the order in which its players perform those draws, so Arturo can draw second and see the partner's card first.
608.2b states that on resolution a spell or ability checks whether its targets are still legal and doesn't resolve if they aren't; Explosion no longer targets Nevaeh or a permanent they control.

510.4 states the second combat damage step is for creatures that had neither first strike nor double strike as the first combat damage step began, so losing first strike afterward doesn't grant another damage assignment.

608.2e states multi-player actions in a resolving spell are chosen in APNAP order and then processed simultaneously, so both cards go to the battlefield at once; 614.12a states a choice required by a replacement effect that modifies how a permanent enters is made before it enters.

118.9 defines alternative costs and 702.34a states flashback is permission to cast the card for a cost instead of its mana cost; 118.9a states only one alternative cost may be applied to a spell, so Nourishing Shoal's own alternative cost can't be added to flashback.

613.7 states later timestamps are applied later, putting Tightening Coils last; 701.3b states attaching something to what it's already attached to does nothing, and 701.3c/613.7e state a new timestamp comes only from becoming attached to a different object.
103.5b states an 'any time you could mulligan' action is taken when that player would declare a mulligan; 103.5 states each player declares in turn order, so Albert acts before Nico has declared.
103.6 states that opening-hand actions like Leyline of Punishment's are taken only once the mulligan process is complete, so they can't be taken before using Serum Powder.
